selection_process: Subject Type of Exam No. of Questions/Components Maximum Marks
General Knowledge Objective 50 questions (1 mark each) 50
English Composition Objective 20 questions (1 mark each) 20
Subjective Essay (150 words) – 10 marks; Letter – 5 marks; Precis – 5 marks; Translation from Punjabi to English – 10 marks 30
Total Marks 100
Selection involves an online written examination
followed by a qualifying Computer Proficiency Test
and finally checking of original testimonials/interaction
with the final merit list based solely on written exam marks.
Duration of the exam is 2 hours. Qualifying marks are 33% in each subject

and a candidate must additionally secure at least 40% marks in aggregate in the Written Examination to be considered to have qualified. There is negative marking of 1/4 mark for every wrong answer in the objective (MCQ) portion; unattempted questions receive no credit or discredit. The subjective English Composition part is checked only for candidates who secure 33% or more marks in General Knowledge.

Candidates who qualify the written exam (numbers decided category-wise by the Hon'ble High Court) are called for a mandatory Computer Proficiency Test; marks from this test are not counted in the final merit
since it is purely qualifying in nature.
Part-I – Spreadsheet Test: 10 marks

10 minutes' duration; candidates must score 40% or more (4 or more marks) to qualify. Part-II – Computer Typing Test (English): Checked only for candidates who clear Part-I; required typing speed is 30 words per minute (WPM)
calculated using the formula: (Number of words typed − Mistakes) ÷ 10.
Specified categories of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities can apply for exemption from the Computer Proficiency Test
along with a Disability Certificate and
where applicable
a Medical Certificate from a Government healthcare institution confirming a physical limitation to type at 30 WPM
submitted within 15 days of the written exam result declaration. The decision of the Competent Authority on exemption is final.
Candidates who qualify both the Written Examination and the Computer Proficiency Test (numbers decided category-wise by the High Court) are called for checking of original testimonials/interaction.

The Select List is prepared strictly on the basis of merit in the Written Examination (Computer Based Test); candidates higher in merit are recommended for appointment as per the number of vacancies to be filled. In case of a tie
the older candidate is ranked higher; if the date of birth is also the same
candidates are placed alphabetically (A–Z).
A provisional Answer Key is published on sssc.gov.in after the written exam
and candidates may raise objections or cross-objections
supported by reasons and documentary proof
on payment of a non-refundable fee of ₹25 per objection. If the written exam is held in multiple shifts
scores in the objective portion are normalised using a Standard Deviation Method

as specified in the notification. Re-evaluation of answer sheets is not allowed; only re-checking (to confirm no part was left unevaluated or there is no totalling error) may be requested in writing within 30 days of the final result
on payment of ₹500 per answer sheet.
how_to_apply: Applications must be submitted online only, under the head "Clerk District Courts of Punjab" on the official website sssc.gov.in. No other mode of submission is accepted. The broad process is:
Registration: Fill the Registration form first, followed by the Application Form.
Real-time photograph: Capture a real-time photograph using an inbuilt or attached webcam, as required within the Online Application Form.
Upload documents: Upload a scanned recent passport-size photograph (not more than one month old, against a white background) and a scanned signature.
Fill in all details carefully: Enter all personal details, including category and sub-category, correctly - no change is permitted after submission.

Pay the fee: The application form is linked to a fee payment gateway (internet banking, debit card, credit card, or UPI); the online application is considered submitted only after successful payment of the fee, which is non-refundable.
Retain documents: Keep a printed copy of the submitted application, and retain 5 copies of the uploaded photograph for later stages of the recruitment process.

Candidates must ensure the real-time photograph, the uploaded scanned photograph, and the photograph pasted on the E-Admit Card all match, and that their facial appearance at the exam matches these photographs - any mismatch means the candidate will not be allowed to enter the examination centre.
important_instructions: All applicants, irrespective of category, can submit only one application for a particular category; if more than one application is submitted, only the latest will be considered. Merely satisfying the eligibility criteria does not entitle an applicant to be called for the examination; admission at every stage is provisional and subject to subsequent scrutiny. Applicants currently in government service must obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their Head of Office/Department and produce it when called for; failure to do so will result in cancellation of candidature. Reservation benefits require applicants to submit the latest, valid certificates issued by the Competent Authority of the Government of Punjab, valid as on the closing date of the application. E-Admit Cards will be uploaded on the website (with E-mail/SMS notification) and must be downloaded by candidates themselves; admit cards are not sent by post. No mobile phone, electronic device, watch, or jewellery/ornaments are allowed inside the examination centre. All applicants must give an undertaking that they will work anywhere in the State of Punjab where posted. Concealing material facts or furnishing false information can lead to rejection of candidature at any stage; canvassing in any form or use of unfair means will lead to cancellation of candidature. No TA/DA is paid for appearing in the exam or for checking of original testimonials/interaction. Success in the examination confers no automatic right to appointment, which remains subject to the Competent Authority's satisfaction regarding the candidate's suitability in all respects.

content_sections.heading: SSSC Punjab Clerk Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: A total of 1,270 posts of Clerk are to be filled. The notification states that the number of vacancies may be increased or decreased without notice, depending on the number of vacancies as on the date of preparation of the merit list and posting; the number of candidates to be recommended will be decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana. Important note on this table: Per the notification, reservation for Sportsman, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen of Punjab operates as horizontal reservation - meaning these candidates are drawn from within the vertical categories (UR/EWS/SC/BC) rather than being counted as fully separate, additional vacancies. Given the complexity of this nested roster and some ambiguity in a few cells when extracting the original table, candidates should treat the figures above as indicative and verify the exact, authoritative category-wise and sub-category-wise vacancy numbers directly from the official notification PDF on sssc.gov.in before applying. Category abbreviations used for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD): LV = Low Vision, HH = Hard of Hearing, OA = One Arm, OL = One Leg, BA = Both Arms, BL = Both Legs, OAL = One Arm and One Leg, LC = Leprosy Cured, Dw = Dwarfism, AAV = Acid Attack Victims, SLD = Specific Learning Disability, MI = Mental Illness, MD = Multiple Disabilities, SD/SI = Spinal Deformity/Spinal Injury.

content_sections.heading: SSSC Punjab Clerk Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The applicant should possess a Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science degree, or an equivalent qualification, from a recognised University. The applicant should also have passed the Matriculation examination with Punjabi as one of the subjects, and must have proficiency in the operation of computers. The applicant must fulfil the qualification condition as on the closing date of the Online Application Form. No person who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living, or who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any other person, shall be eligible for appointment - unless the Hon'ble High Court is satisfied that such a marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to such a person and exempts them from this rule. Reservation benefits, age relaxation, and fee concessions are available only to bonafide residents of the State of Punjab (except age relaxation for government employees, as provided in the Rules); applicants from reserved categories of other states must apply under the Unreserved (UR)/General category. Reservation is regulated as per The Punjab Subordinate Courts Establishment (Recruitment and General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1997, as amended, along with specific Punjab Government instructions governing EWS, Women, Sportsman, Freedom Fighter, and PwBD reservation categories. If sufficient candidates are not available in a particular reserved category, unfilled vacancies in that category may be filled from the unreserved category, subject to availability.

faq.question: Q1. What is SSSC Punjab Clerk Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is Detailed Employment Notice No. 37C/SSSC/PB/2026, issued by the Society for Centralized Recruitment of Staff in Subordinate Courts under the High Court of Punjab and Haryana, for direct recruitment to 1,270 Clerk posts in the District Courts of Punjab.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in SSSC Punjab Clerk Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 1,270 posts of Clerk, distributed across Unreserved, EWS, SC, BC/OBC, Freedom Fighter, Sportsman, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen categories of Punjab. See the Vacancy section above for the detailed category-wise breakup.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for SSSC Punjab Clerk Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application closing date is 4 November 2026, 4:00 PM.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for SSSC Punjab Clerk?
faq.answer: A Bachelor's degree (BA/B.Sc or equivalent) from a recognised university, a pass in Matriculation with Punjabi as a subject, and proficiency in computer operation.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for SSSC Punjab Clerk Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The general age limit is 18–37 years as on 1 January 2026, with relaxation of 5 years for SC/BC-OBC, 10 years for PwBD, and up to military service plus 3 years for Ex-Servicemen, all of Punjab.

faq.question: Q6. What is the SSSC Punjab Clerk application fee?
faq.answer: ₹710 for SC/BC/OBC/ESM/EWS of Punjab, ₹875 for PwBD of Punjab, and ₹1,200 for all other categories.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for SSSC Punjab Clerk Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted online only at sssc.gov.in under "Clerk District Courts of Punjab," between 7 October 2026 and 4 November 2026, as described in the How to Apply section above.

faq.question: Q8. What is the SSSC Punjab Clerk selection process?
faq.answer: Selection involves a 100-mark online written exam (General Knowledge and English Composition), followed by a qualifying Computer Proficiency Test, and checking of original testimonials/interaction, with the final merit list based solely on written exam marks, as detailed in the Selection Process section above.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary for SSSC Punjab Clerk?
faq.answer: The pay scale is Level-5, ₹29,200 per month for Graduates, for fresh recruitment/appointment on or after 17 July 2020.
